items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: And so I was listening to the two of them and the other two trombone players and we kind of locked together. You know Dennis Wilson, he was a perfectly well trained musician.

ctx.x: Well the Count Basie band I kind of knew. I kind of knew what they were doing and how they were doing it. In fact the way I got to keep the Basie gig is because I listened to Bill

Hughes, the bass trombone player. And he would kind of lead the band from the bottom. And Mel Wanzo wasn’t the best trombone player in the world but he could play that music the way it was supposed to be played. You know? And so I was listening to the two of them and the other two trombone players and we kind of locked together. You know Dennis Wilson, he was a perfectly well trained musician. He wrote arrangements with a ball point pen. Full band arrangements and he never made a mistake. And I just admired that…

In the arranging you’ve done, if you think back on it, I’m wondering if something, an artist or a situation comes to your mind that was really challenging and that stretched what you had been doing previously, if it’s writing for strings or something like that.
